strategy_name: Consensus vs actual news surprise (buy the rumor, sell the news)
mechanism: large players pre-position for consensus expectations before data release, so only the deviation of actual from consensus moves price - matching news produces reversals, surprising news produces one-way moves
setup_summary: Around scheduled releases, track consensus forecasts: if actual > forecast the currency tends to strengthen (actual worse than forecast => downward pressure); if actual == consensus expect little or reverse movement because positioning was completed pre-release. The 'sell the news' case is a fade of the pre-release run-up.
trigger_invalidation: No trade when actual matches consensus; thesis invalid if price does not move in the surprise direction in the post-release window.
risk_geometry: Book specifies none; news wicks imply entry at bar close after the release with stop beyond the initial spike.
quote: The currency rates often start moving even before the actual data comes out due to forecasts and market sentiment! ... If the actual data comes out worse than expected, it creates a strong downward pressure on the currency.
chapter_anchor: Section 02, Consensus Vs Actual numbers (reference: babypips)
notes: BTC has no own macro calendar but is highly sensitive to US CPI/FOMC releases; the surprise-vs-consensus mechanism is testable in principle, but V8's tape does not carry consensus/surprise data, so this is DATA_BLOCKED until a news/surprise feed exists. Narrative worked example (consensus 9.0%, actual 9.0% => no move; 8.0% => dollar rally; 10.0% => drop), no statistics.
book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

strategy_name: Leverage/tax-neutral cheapness metric: EBIT/EV instead of P/E or E/P
setup_summary: When comparing how cheap assets are, deflate operating earnings by enterprise value (equity price + net interest-bearing debt), not by equity price alone: P/E and E/P are distorted by differing debt levels and tax rates, while EBIT/EV is not. The book's worked example: two identical businesses (same EBIT 10, Company A no debt at $60, Company B $50 debt at $10) have the same EBIT/EV yield (10/60) despite P/E of 10 vs 3.33.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any cheapness/rank comparison across assets with different leverage must normalize to a leverage-neutral yield. Invalidation: raw price- or margin-based yield ranking misranks assets whenever leverage differs across the universe.
risk_geometry: n/a - metric-construction methodology feeding any cross-asset ranker.
quote: P/E and E/P are greatly influenced by changes in debt levels and tax rates, while EBIT/EV is not.
chapter_anchor: Appendix p.143-145 (definitions p.139-142)
notes: Perps embed leverage by construction (margin vs notional), so a funding/carry-based cheapness ranking across instruments should normalize yield to total notional exposure rather than to mark price or margin - the direct analog of EBIT/EV vs P/E. Applies only if V8 adds cross-instrument carry ranking.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Roll-over cost as carry input
setup_summary: Glossary definition of Roll-Over: settlement of a deal is rolled forward to another value date, and the cost of this process is based on the interest-rate differential of the two currencies. This is the FX roll-over concept; in crypto perpetuals the direct analogue is the funding rate paid to hold a position across funding intervals. Falsifiable: holding-cost differential is observable and priced into the instrument.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - structural cost definition rather than a trigger; applies whenever a position is held across a roll/funding event.
risk_geometry: Cost of carry: interest-rate differential (FX) / funding rate (perps); affects PnL of held positions and discourages long holding when carry is adverse.
quote: Roll-Over Process whereby the settlement of a deal is rolled forward to another value date. The cost of this process is based on the interest rate differential of the two currencies.
chapter_anchor: Glossary entry 'Roll-Over'
notes: Direct structural mapping to crypto perp funding; motivates funding-rate as a feature (flow group) and as carry-cost input to expert PnL in the simulator's cost model.

strategy_name: Funding carry trade and carry unwind (Icelandic krona carry)
mechanism: Leveraged carry positions are paid to hold an appreciating, high-yield asset funded in a cheap currency; the position is self-reinforcing while the target appreciates, but unwinds violently and herding-driven when the funding mismatch reverses.
setup_summary: Book setup (falsifiable on perp data): households borrowed yen at ~3% and Swiss francs to buy krona-yield assets paying 15.5% while the krona rose; the trade was profitable until the carry target collapsed, at which point the funding-currency obligations became multiples more expensive (gap-like repricing; krona removed from the market). Perp analog: when perp funding is persistently and unusually positive while price trends up, leveraged longs are collectively paid to hold; the falsifiable claim is that such carry crowding is fragile and the unwind is a liquidation cascade once price breaks the carry-trend low or funding flips sharply negative.
trigger_invalidation: Carry thesis invalid when the carry target stops appreciating (price breaks its carry-trend support) or the funding/carry spread reverses; book event: krona collapsed and yen/Swiss-franc obligations repriced multiples higher.
risk_geometry: No explicit stop or target in the book; the documented failure mode is gap-like repricing (FX market suspended), which in perps maps to a funding-driven liquidation waterfall rather than a price gap (24/7 venue).
quote: With local interest rates at 15.5 percent and the krona rising, they decided the smart thing to do, when they wanted to buy something they couldn't afford, was to borrow not kronur but yen and Swiss francs. ... in October, after the krona collapsed, the yen and Swiss francs they must repay became many times more expensive.
chapter_anchor: Part I, 'Wall Street on the Tundra' (Icelandic carry-trade section, ~44/396)
notes: Funding carry is first-class perp microstructure (funding rate, leverage, 24/7). Requires funding-rate data; funding is not currently a frozen feature group, so this is DATA_BLOCKED/backlog until a funding feature group exists. Distinguish from the simpler 'collect funding while long' trade: the edge claim here is that extreme carry crowding predicts its own violent unwind.
book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

strategy_name: Performance-chasing penalty: dollar-weighted investor returns lag asset returns
mechanism: Crowd flow follows recent performance: money flows into funds after good performance and out after bad, so the average participant buys high and sells low; dollar-weighted investor returns lag time-weighted fund returns by ~2.7pp/yr industry-wide and ~8.3pp/yr for the hottest aggressive funds.
setup_summary: After large recent gains, inflows spike and subsequent dollar-weighted returns fall short of reported returns; hot sector ETF shareholders lagged their funds by ~5pp/yr (only 1 of 20 top ETFs 2003-06 gave shareholders the reported return). A falsifiable fade: measure flow proxy (funding premium, OI growth, net taker buy-flow) after a large N-bar rally; strongly positive flow while price is extended predicts below-average forward returns.
trigger_invalidation: Setup does not apply when flow is neutral or negative after the rally (crowd already rotated); if the move is genuinely fundamental, the chase continues and the fade loses.
risk_geometry: Contrarian fade: entry on flow-extreme signal after extension, stop beyond the move's structure, target = reversion to mean flow level; the penalty scales with how hot the chased asset is (index fund investors lagged 2.0pp vs 8.3pp for aggressive funds).
quote: Hint: money flows into most funds after good performance, and goes out when bad performance follows.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 (The Grand Illusion, Exhibits 5.2-5.3), Chapter 15 (ETFs: shareholder shortfall ~5pp/yr)
notes: Funding rate, OI delta and taker flow are directly observable perp analogs of fund flows; this is the book's most directly tradeable phenomenon, though it is documented as a penalty, not a prescribed fade - keep as backlog candidate until flow tape exists.
book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

strategy_name: Consecutive up/down closes exhaustion trail (sentiment-extreme exit)
mechanism: x consecutive closes in one direction indicate near-complete agreement (too many on one side of the boat); the run is at a sentiment extreme and reversal/at-least consolidation follows
setup_summary: After 8 consecutive closes in the same direction (weekly or daily), treat the trend as at a sentiment extreme: if long, place a stop just below the low of the last up-bar and trail it one bar at a time as the streak extends; exit when stopped. If the streak ends without the prior bar's extreme being taken out, continue holding. Exit is the primary use — this is an exit/timing rule, not an entry rule.
trigger_invalidation: Activation after an 8-bar streak; trail continues while each new bar extends; invalidated/exit when a bar takes out the prior bar's extreme. The '8' threshold is a starting point to be recalibrated per timeframe.
risk_geometry: Entry: none (exit rule). Stop: prior bar low (long) / prior bar high (short), trailed each bar. No target — exit at the extreme. Book examples: DXY bottom after 11 consecutive down weeks (Dec 2004); EURUSD tops after 9 and 8 consecutive up weeks (Jan/Dec 2004); USDCAD turns after ~9-week streaks.
quote: Use 8 as a starting point. For example, once a pair has rallied for 8 weeks (or days), place a stop just below the low of the last week.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, When to Get Out — Consecutive Up and Down Periods, pp. 146-149
notes: On BTCUSDT 1h, 8 consecutive up-hours occurs frequently; the streak threshold and bar size must be recalibrated (book uses weekly/daily). Best used as a stop-trailing rule inside an existing trend-following expert rather than a standalone entry.
book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

strategy_name: Technical carry trade: positive-yield position entered only near long-term support/resistance
mechanism: Capital flows toward higher-yielding currencies when risk appetite is not extreme; a carry trader earns the (leveraged) interest differential daily. Technical carry adds a location filter: entry near long-term support (long carry) or resistance (short carry) is the high-probability zone, cutting adverse-move risk.
setup_summary: Screen pairs for a large current interest-rate differential (threshold ~300 bp) and its likely future direction from central-bank policy. Then select only pairs whose price is in the bottom third of the long-term vertical range (for long carry) or near long-term resistance (for short carry). Scale entry with multiple fractional positions spaced evenly across the support zone; target the top third of the range; stop below long-term support.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pair with positive carry differential and price in the high-probability location (near support/resistance). Invalidation: differential shrinks/reverses (rate-cycle turn); stop below long-term support; adverse price moves can erase all daily interest gains.
risk_geometry: Entry: scaled/fractional entries across the bottom-third support zone. Stop: just below long-term support. Target: top third of the long-term range (technically based). Holding period: long-term (weeks to months); daily interest settled at rollover on the FULL leveraged notional, not just margin.
quote: if a substantial positive interest rate differential can be achieved by buying a currency pair... the highest probability entry would be near long-term support. When price on the pair is near long-term support, the historical probability is that price should eventually rise.
chapter_anchor: Ch4 'Carried Away with Trading' pp.108-110; Ch5 'Technical Carry Trade' Tips & Techniques pp.181-182
notes: In perps, the interest differential maps to the funding rate (paid on full notional, continuous, no central-bank cycle). Key differences: funding is small, sign-flips, and long-carry is exposed to deleveraging cascades. The transferable piece is the location filter (enter near long-term support) — a candidate REFINE for trend_pullback requiring a cross_market funding feature (derivatives tape, DATA_BLOCKED today).
book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

strategy_name: Contrarian fade of extreme speculator net positioning (COT / positioning extremes)
mechanism: When large speculators' net positioning reaches an extreme, the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted — there is little uncommitted capital left to push price further, so price is prone to reverse.
setup_summary: Monitor net speculator positioning (CFTC COT report for FX futures; mass-media consensus as a proxy). When major speculators are drastically and increasingly net long at a recent peak, prepare to short; when net short at an extreme, prepare to buy. The contrarian premise: media and consensus are usually wrong or extremely late at market extremes.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: positioning at a recent extreme peak/trough. Invalidation: positioning keeps extending (contrarian trades can step in front of a trend); book explicitly warns this is risky and needs strict risk controls — 'do not step into the path of a speeding train'.
risk_geometry: Entry: on positioning extreme (bar-close after confirmation). Stop: not specified (book defers specific COT methods 'beyond the scope'); V8 geometry must be added (ATR/swing-based). Target: mean-reversion toward prior range; no expiry stated.
quote: if the COT report shows that major speculators have been drastically and increasingly net long in the British pound against the U.S. dollar... traders may begin looking for the next opportunity to short the pound in a classic contrarian maneuver.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Contrarian Trading—The Majority Doesn't Rule', pp.184-187 (COT report p.185, Exhibit 5.16 p.186)
notes: No COT equivalent in perps; proxies are venue long/short ratios, aggregate open interest, and funding-rate extremes — noisy, venue-specific, and not yet in the V8 tape. Best use is a participation/flow feature input and a regime-level contrarian filter, not a standalone expert. Class sentiment (positioning extremes), maps to existing V8 vocab flow/participation feature groups.
book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

strategy_name: Text-mining sentiment polarity and risk-appetite/aversion ratio
mechanism: crowd opinion is measurable from text; sentiment crossovers mark opinion shifts and sentiment peaks (positive or negative) are milestones for subsequent price reversals
setup_summary: Mine headlines/keywords for a market (seed terms: 'risk appetite', 'risk aversion', + market + emotional adjective/adverb), score each hit -5..+5, and build a positive/negative sentiment ratio; treat polarity crossover and extreme sentiment peaks as regime/shift signals. Book cites research: topic-based Twitter sentiment improved next-day S&P 100 prediction; WSJ text mining claimed >55.7% accuracy on daily direction. For crypto perps the analog is funding/OI/extreme positioning plus social sentiment, but the book's own caution applies: Twitter-grade data is at best a confirming indicator.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sentiment polarity crossover, or sentiment score at a rolling extreme. Invalidation: sentiment continues to diverge from price (no confirmation); the polarity signal is treated only as confirming, never standalone.
risk_geometry: Not a price-geometry trade in V8; input to regime/direction filters only. Book uses it to choose binary moneyness (OTM when central-bank statement due, since surprise risk is high).
quote: sentiment peaks, whether positive or negative, are the key milestones relating to subsequent price changes and offer great potential as a source of trading signals.
notes: LITERATURE_SUPPORTED because the chapter cites peer-style studies (Si et al. 2013 Twitter; Wong, Liu, Chiang 2014 WSJ >55.7%; Hafez/RavenPack). V8 has no 'sentiment' feature group in the frozen vocabulary - would need a registry decision to add one, or proxy via funding/OI (flow). Book's 'binaries misprice OTM ladders because market makers cannot price extremes' (Ch 1, pp. 16-17) is an edge claim specific to the $100-payoff market and NOT transferable to perps.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Carry trade via interest-rate differentials
mechanism: capital flows to where expected yields are highest; selling low-rate and buying high-rate instruments harvests the differential (the 'jet stream' of currency flows)
setup_summary: Currencies strengthen when their central bank's rates are expected to rise and weaken when expected to fall; the carry trade sells low-rate currencies (JPY, CHF, USD) and buys high-rate (AUD, NZD), with the warning that an overextended high-rate currency eventually self-corrects. Crypto-perp mapping: funding rate is the closest analog - sustained positive funding signals crowded longs paying carry (fade candidates), negative funding the reverse; venue-to-venue funding spreads can be traded. Book adds: when a central-bank statement is due, prefer OTM (surprise risk), and rate expectations, not current rates, drive price.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sustained funding/rate differential regime. Invalidation: central-bank policy shift flips expectations; crowding self-correction unwinds the carry (see carry_unwind).
risk_geometry: No entry/stop geometry in V8 terms; a flow/regime feature rather than a per-trade setup. Book: high-rate carry is cyclical and self-correcting - do not hold extreme positions.
quote: This leads to a strategy called the carry trade. This strategy involves selling low interest rate currencies... and then buying high interest rate currencies. ... interest rate differentials can be considered the jet stream of the currency market!
notes: The FX-rate-differential mechanism is not directly tradeable in single-instrument perps, but funding-rate regimes are a real, measurable perp feature (crowding signal + carry cost); propose as a flow-group input and a regime filter, not an expert.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Put/call ratio as contrarian sentiment/positioning gauge
mechanism: positioning-extreme contrarian: extreme put/call ratios (heavy bearish options positioning) mark contrarian-bullish conditions and extreme call-heavy readings mark complacency/contrarian-bearish conditions
setup_summary: Track sector/index put/call ratios as a positioning gauge; extreme readings are contrarian signals. Perp analog: funding rate + open interest positioning as the perp-native crowd-positioning gauge (heavy long positioning via high positive funding = contrarian-short; flush to negative funding = contrarian-long).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: positioning gauge crosses an extreme threshold. Invalidation: positioning stays/extends (no mean reversion of the gauge within N bars).
risk_geometry: Feature/filter input; no own entry geometry - feeds a regime filter or confirmation for direction.
quote: Put/call ratios, 115-117; Sector put/call ratios, 115-117; Fear and Greed index, 115
chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 115-117 (put/call ratios, option volatility and sentiment)
notes: The options put/call ratio maps imperfectly to perp (no put/call tape), but funding rate + OI is the perp-native positioning gauge with the same contrarian logic; fund-flow group already in vocabulary. Keep as feature input; the contrarian claim is falsifiable on funding extremes.

strategy_name: Swap and Fly (carry with break-even stop)
mechanism: Holding a position in the direction of a positive interest-rate differential accrues swap daily; once the trade moves 1R, shifting the stop to break-even converts it into a risk-free swap accumulator whose P&L turns positive purely from the accrual.
setup_summary: On D1/W1, select the pair with the highest positive swap in the trade direction (book: long AUD/JPY, short GBP/AUD on FXPRIMUS). Enter at the opening of the next candle after a three-white-soldiers (long) or three-black-crows (short) pattern; stop at the recent significant low/high; once the trade reaches 1:1 R, shift the stop to break-even; hold until stopped, accruing swap daily (example: AUD/JPY long accrued 302 pips of swap over 36 weeks). Optional full exit at a minimum 1:3 R.
trigger_invalidation: Stopped at the significant swing before reaching 1:1 R (no break-even shift); the carry accrual is the thesis, so it fails if swap/funding direction reverts (book: swap 'moves in tandem with central banks' rates').
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open after 3-candle pattern; stop at recent significant swing; dynamic stop shift to break-even at 1R; no fixed target (swap accumulation); expiry: weeks-months.
quote: The swap and fly strategy is a slow but steady technique that helps you to accumulate interest every day. You can even come out with a positive return after a period of time, even though the trade exits at breakeven.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Strategy 12 'Swap and Fly', pp. 192-199
notes: The break-even stop shift at 1R is the transferable lifecycle rule (consistent with V8's separation of stops vs dead-thesis exits). In crypto perps the analog is funding, but funding settles every 8h, is frequently negative for longs in BTC, and has no central-bank persistence - so this is NOT the same edge; a crypto funding_carry expert is data-blocked until funding data exists and would need an inverted-direction handling.
book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

strategy_name: Swap and Fly (carry capture with breakeven-shifted stop)
mechanism: Holding a position that earns positive interest/funding generates profit by time alone once the trade reaches breakeven; the carry accrual replaces the need for price appreciation
setup_summary: On D1/W1, select the pair with the highest positive swap on the intended side (book: long AUD/JPY, short GBP/AUD). Enter on a three-white-soldiers (long) or three-black-crows (short) candle pattern at the open of the next candle; stop at a recent significant low/high. When price reaches +1R, shift the stop to entry (breakeven); hold until the breakeven stop is hit - swap accrued over weeks makes the exit profitable (book example: ~1.2 pips/week swap, breakeven after 36 weeks).
trigger_invalidation: Stop hit before price reaches +1R (no breakeven shift possible).
risk_geometry: Entry at next-bar open after pattern; stop at recent swing; shift stop to entry at +1R; no target (hold for carry); optional full exit at >=1:3 R.
quote: After a period of time, even if our 'new' stop-loss level is hit, the trade is exited with a profit because of the swap earned.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Strategy 12 (Swap and Fly), pp. 192-199
notes: The perp analog is funding: hold BTCUSDT long while funding is positive (or short when negative), shift stop to BE at +1R, let funding accrue. Directly uses the V8 'flow' feature group (funding). DATA_BLOCKED until a funding-rate feed is added to the tape. Swap rates are broker/time-varying - same caveat applies to perp funding.

strategy_name: Roll yield decay / cost drag on passive futures and CTAs
mechanism: Strategy edge that comes from a structural premium (roll yield paid by hedgers) decays as speculators crowd in; passive/fee-heavy futures vehicles can net near-zero or negative excess return after carry and front-running costs.
setup_summary: Lesson with falsifiable numbers: commodity futures roll return averaged +11%/yr (1969-1992) but -6.6%/yr since 2001 as noncommercial open interest rose from 15% to 42%; front-running of index rolls cost ~3.6%/yr (Mou 2011); 930 CTAs netted ~1.8%/yr over T-bills 1994-2012 (not significantly different from zero, Bhardwaj et al.) while fees averaged 4.3%/yr; Marshall et al. (2008) found no profitability across 7,000 rules in 5 families on 15 commodity markets.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - cost/methodology lesson. Falsifiable claim: crowding erodes premium-type edges over time (also seen with the size premium disappearing post-1980s).
risk_geometry: None; the operative rule is to model every recurring cost (funding, spread, taker fees, roll-equivalent) and to distrust strategies whose modeled edge is small vs. cost drag.
quote: From 1969 to 1992, the roll return averaged 11% per year. Since 2001, it has averaged a negative 6.6%.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Asset Selection (Passive Commodity Futures and Managed Commodity Futures)
notes: Crypto-perp analog: perps have no roll (no expiry), but funding is a standing carry cost and perp carry strategies face the same crowding decay the book documents for roll yield; additionally the book shows the trend-overlay alternative (Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen absolute momentum across 58 futures) matched CTA results before fees - reinforcing absolute momentum as the low-cost baseline. V8-native: simulator cost model must include funding; evaluation must show edge is material after costs.
book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

strategy_name: Five-of-six method portfolio rotation (Pareto culling)
mechanism: Returns concentration (Pareto/80-20): ~90% of profit comes from ~10% of methods, so a portfolio that periodically culls its worst-performing method and adds a new candidate steadily improves performance.
setup_summary: Run six methods concurrently; at each annual review drop the worst-performing method and add a new one, keeping the top five. Author reports his analysis showed about 90% of profits came from 10% of his ~40 systems, and expects ~10%/yr performance gains from relentless culling.
trigger_invalidation: Rotation assumes the worst performer is identifiable on frozen, out-of-sample evidence rather than luck (needs a fair sample before culling), and that replacement candidates are continuously available; invalid if culling sacrifices genuine diversification.
risk_geometry: None — portfolio-level process, not a trade-level rule.
quote: you will be constantly improving your trading performance by relentlessly throwing out the worst-performing method and keeping the top five... Actually, about 90 percent was coming from 10 percent of the systems!
chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Keep the Top Five, Drop the Worst / Keep Your Trading to 15 Minutes a Day (pp. 165, 169)
notes: Maps directly to V8's registry lifecycle: worst-performing family on frozen OOS -> QUARANTINED/REJECTED, new family enters as PROPOSED. V8's max-3 ACTIVE experts caps simultaneous breadth, so the lesson applies to registry turnover velocity, not running six families at once.

strategy_name: Fade-the-public sentiment filter
mechanism: Short-term public positioning is systematically wrong; when the crowd is excessively long or short, the informed side is the opposite, so extreme public stance disqualifies aligned entries
setup_summary: Falsifiable filter, not a standalone signal: use post-close short-term-trader surveys (Jake Bernstein) and newsletter-writer sentiment (Market Vane, longer-horizon) as a disqualifier — never enter a trade with an extreme public stance on the same side; align only against it. Williams: 'If the public is excessive in their selling, I don't want to be a seller along with them.' For crypto perps the survey data does not exist; the analogues are funding-rate extremes and long/short-account ratios, which also act as carry flows.
trigger_invalidation: Sentiment extremes are descriptive; invalidation = crowd being right for a sustained stretch
risk_geometry: Filter only; no standalone entry/stop/target
quote: If the public is excessive in their selling, I don't want to be a seller along with them. I may not always fade the public, but I sure don't want them on my side of the table.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'The Theory of Short-Term Trading' (pp. 75-77)
notes: No quantitative test in the book (80%-lose claim is anecdotal). Backlog candidate: funding-rate / long-short-ratio extreme as a participation+flow feature, evaluated against V8's own data before any expert uses it.

strategy_name: High-watermark trailing stop, never-average-down, and overtrading caps
mechanism: Raising the stop at each new closing extreme locks in gains and lets winners run; proscribing averaging-down and capping trade frequency blocks the two classic loser behaviors (add-to-loser, revenge trading).
setup_summary: Adjust stops and targets once per day on a high-watermark basis: raise the stop-loss at each new closing high since entry (new low for shorts); lower the target at each new adverse low (raise for shorts). Preferred profit exit is the trailing stop moved on a closing basis ('let your winners run') — the two or three huge winners per year carry the account. Never average down on a losing position (keep the stop, lower the target, wait). Never overtrade: set a daily profit point or trade-count cap and stop for the day when reached; scale back size during a losing streak, increase during a winning streak; beginners cap position at ~1/10 of the account.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — position-management layer; the book allows exceptions only 'as dictated by current market conditions.'
risk_geometry: Stop moved only at end of day on closing basis (avoid intraday whipsaw); in equities, take stops off overnight but keep target limit orders in place; target orders can be broken into small bits one penny apart.
quote: raise your stop-loss price at each new closing high since entry (or new low if the trade is a short)... Never average down on a losing position.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 habits 2,3,8,9 (pp. 84-89) + Ch. 11 'Entries and Exits' (pp. 229-239)
notes: For V8: closing-basis trailing-stop raises are a lifecycle/exposure-book rule operating on frozen refs + still_valid (the 'adjust at end of day' becomes a fixed UTC anchor such as the funding hour or session close, never wall-clock inside replay). Never-average-down aligns with rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument/direction) and the no-add-to-loser convention. Trade-count caps and scale-down-after-losses are RiskGate/position-sizing candidates. The trailing stop vs fixed-target tradeoff: fixed targets give steady cash flow but 'you then miss out on those few big runs that, in themselves, can be all the fuel you need to get your account into the big leagues.'
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Leveraged carry blowup: correlation breakdown plus mis-estimated tail
mechanism: A small positive-carry spread multiplied by leverage and 'protected' by hedges blows up when hedges break down together and the tail probability was mis-estimated from short history (the 'ten sigma' error)
setup_summary: John's trade: borrow at ~5.5%, buy ~10% 'cheap' bonds (net 4.5% carry), hedge interest-rate exposure with government-bond futures, levered to ~$50M book on ~$14M equity. The 1998 event: everything went against him at once, hedges failed together, and the model put the event at 'ten sigma' (1 in 10^24 years). The book's lesson: model-derived probabilities from recent history understate rare-event frequency by orders of magnitude, and correlation breakdown under stress invalidates the hedge.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: leveraged carry with hedges. Invalid: hedges exhibit correlation breakdown under stress (correlations go to 1), carry flips, or realized tail frequency exceeds the model estimate.
risk_geometry: Entry: long carry asset / short hedge (futures); leverage ~3.6x implied; stop: none effective; target: carry yield plus convergence; expiry: ongoing; failure mode: leveraged unwind. Note: 'a small loss would be compounded and would wipe him out'.
quote: The effect of the leverage is that a small loss would be compounded and would wipe him out.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, The Quant Who Knew Computers and Equations (p. 76-77)
notes: Crypto analog is direct: funding carry and basis trades are native to perps, leverage is extreme, and deleveraging cascades/flash crashes are documented. Maps to correlated_exposure_cap and max_drawdown_cap rules, plus a simulator requirement to model stress correlation breakdown rather than permanent hedge offset. The 'ten sigma' point also feeds the stationarity finding (NEW_crowded_pattern_stationarity).

strategy_name: Consensus narrative overriding price (firehouse effect)
mechanism: A narrative shared and reinforced among peers ('it's only a liquidation', 'sell-off is overdone', 'too big to fail') anchors the thesis and overrides price evidence; the price is the un-fooled referee
setup_summary: Anti-pattern: Carlos's hour-long daily calls with market economists all saying 'this sell-off is overdone' and 'Russia will not go under', plus self-justification via 'other banks have bigger losses' (the firehouse effect: people who talk to each other too long come to agree on things an outside observer finds ludicrous). The thesis was never anchored to price; the bonds fell from $52 to below $10. Lesson: keep thesis invalidation strictly price-based; narrative/story inputs cannot override price evidence, and a statement 'that other traders also got into trouble' is self-incriminating.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: thesis supported only by narrative. Invalid: price action violates the narrative-anchored level; 'overdone' stories coincide with continued price decline.
risk_geometry: n/a — behavioral/methodology lesson.

strategy_name: Time-series momentum driven by persistence of the roll-return (carry) sign
mechanism: when carry (roll yield) dominates and keeps its sign, total returns acquire serial correlation; in crypto perps the funding rate is the carry
setup_summary: Futures time-series momentum (buy a future with a positive 12-month return, hold ~1 month; Moskowitz-Yao-Pedersen) is largely explained by the persistence of the sign of roll returns rather than spot moves. Cleaner signal: go long when the lagged annualized roll return exceeds a threshold (3% for TU), short when below -threshold, flat otherwise - TU APR 2.5%, Sharpe 2.1, max DD 1.1%. Crypto analog: perp funding rate; persistent positive funding (perps above spot) predicts continued perp outperformance.
trigger_invalidation: Carry sign flips or carry magnitude collapses; regime shifts such as post-crisis momentum crashes.
risk_geometry: Time-based exit: fixed holding period (~25 bars); a stop-loss is consistent with this family (unlike mean reversion).
quote: Typically, the sign of roll returns does not vary very often... So if we hold a future over a long period of time, and if the average roll returns dominate the average total returns, we will find serial correlation of total returns.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'Time Series Strategies' + Chapter 5, 'Roll Returns, Backwardation, and Contango' (Example 6.1, Table 6.2)

strategy_name: Sector risk cap (5% of portfolio per sector)
mechanism: positions within one correlated sector are effectively one risk, so summing them understates true portfolio risk
setup_summary: Cap aggregate risk allocated to any one sector (e.g., interest rates, grains, tech) at 5% of portfolio. Do not take a new trade if it would push that sector's summed risk above 5%. Sectors = correlated groups (gold->silver, soybeans->corn->wheat, tech shares).

strategy_name: Inverse-correlation cross-pair hedge
mechanism: Pairing a directional position with an inversely correlated instrument reduces combined variance; the hedge pays off precisely when the primary thesis fails
setup_summary: Book's 'advanced strategy': long AUD/USD hedged with a JPY/EUR position chosen from a correlation matrix (weekly inverse correlation -50.9%); 'while the performance of the AUD/USD and JPY/EUR have varied since 2007, their combined return has always been positive' - i.e., the combination had lower drawdown and still-positive cumulative return across the credit crisis. The book stresses causation vs. correlation: only causation (not mere co-movement) is actionable, and correlations strengthened over time partly due to cross-asset algorithms and index flows.
trigger_invalidation: Hedge thesis invalidates when the rolling correlation breaks down or flips sign (book notes EM currency correlations broke down in H2 2010 as growth/inflation differentials diverged); a stale correlation matrix is dangerous.
risk_geometry: Hedge sizing, not an entry setup: leg sizes chosen so combined exposure is net-neutral on the shared risk factor; no expiry in the book beyond periodic re-correlation checks.

strategy_name: Rollover/carry on the interest-rate differential

Rollover is automatic and continuous (some brokers compute it every second), so it is a standing drag or tailwind on every held position.

strategy_name: Contango/rollover and leveraged-ETF daily-reset decay
mechanism: Rolling expiring futures into dearer forward months (contango) and daily re-leveraging of leveraged/inverse products both impose a structural, compounding drag on buy-and-hold, so the vehicle systematically underperforms the index it tracks.
setup_summary: Quantified decay: USO fell ~48% from inception (2006) to mid-2011 vs -30.1% for E-mini crude (~18% underperformance in 5 years); UNG similarly underperformed natural-gas futures; over H1-2009 the S&P 500 returned +3.16% while a 2x long returned -0.68%, a 1x inverse -8.91%, and a 2x inverse -21.68% - all from daily resets/rolls, not from index direction. Commodities with easy physical delivery (gold, silver) escape the roll drag. Front-running speculators and 'rollover' each month mechanically guarantee the loss. Lesson for V8: funding on perps is the structural analog - persistent positive funding is a roll-like drag on longs; the simulator's Binance USDM cost model must price funding and basis, and any multi-leverage or inverse construction must not be treated as a 1x underlying.

strategy_name: Dual time-stop + price-stop rule for carry-negative positions
mechanism: positions that bleed carry every day must be bounded by the lesser of a price stop and a time stop - the clock is the enemy when carry is negative
setup_summary: Risk rule: for any position with negative time/carry cost (book: long option premium; perp analog: paying funding, or holding a thesis that pays funding against you), quantify BOTH the price risk and the time risk before entry and exit when the lesser of the two is reached. Movement of the underlying works in the trader's favor; movement of the clock does not.
trigger_invalidation: Exit when either the preset price stop or the preset time stop is hit, whichever comes first.
risk_geometry: Dual stops defined at entry: price stop on the position and time stop (calendar date / bar count); exit on the lesser of the two.
quote: It is important to set both price and time constraints on these types of positions. It is important to quantify the price risk and the time risk you are willing to take before the trade is made and exit when the lesser of the two is reached.

strategy_name: 'Rate of return is a trap' - yield is risk compensation, not edge
mechanism: premium/carry yield is the market's price for perceived risk, not a standalone edge; elevated yield only signals that participants expect larger moves
setup_summary: Methodology lesson: never select an income/premium-selling strategy on the basis of its rate of return or premium yield alone. The rate of return is 'simply an indicator of the risk level perceived by market participants' - high premiums mean participants have built in the possibility of larger moves. The underlying price forecast must be the first determining factor. Direct perp analog: do not select funding-carry trades purely because funding is high; the carry is compensation for the directional and liquidation risk the market prices in.

risk_geometry: N/A - methodology; shapes selection and sizing, not entry/stop geometry.

strategy_name: Fund selling exhaustion divergence bottom
mechanism: Funds are positive-feedback traders; when price makes a new low but the fund net position refuses to make a new low (higher bottom), speculative selling is provably subsiding - exhaustion - tipping a major bottom.
setup_summary: Weekly: during a downtrend, price prints a new low while the large-speculator net position forms a higher bottom than its prior extreme. This is a momentum-style non-confirmation but on positioning data, and the book calls it 'proof positive' that speculative selling is subsiding: bank short profits and take an early long entry into the new uptrend.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price new low + fund net position higher bottom. Invalidation: fund net position also makes a new low (no divergence); also, trend changes at D/Z only count when funds stop short of their previous extremes.
risk_geometry: Early long entry at the divergence; stop and target not specified; Ch 10 adds: if funds hold a near-record net position in the trend direction, tighten the trailing stop rather than trying to pick the exact top/bottom.
quote: In the case of the fund net position, it is not just a sign; it is proof positive that speculative selling is subsiding.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Net Positions, Figure 5.8 (Fund Selling Exhaustion Marks a Major Bottom)
notes: Refines the existing capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion) with a positioning-divergence variant: in crypto, OI/funding divergence at a price low (e.g., funding deeply negative while OI falls / long interest already flushed) is observable on the 1h tape. strategy_name: Backwardation roll yield / funding carry
mechanism: Hedgers pay a risk premium to speculators (hedging pressure); in backwardation, long positions earn a roll yield as deferred futures converge up to spot, while contango guarantees a roll loss for longs - carry is a return source independent of price direction.
setup_summary: Observable weekly/monthly: term-structure sign (backwardation vs contango) or funding-rate sign determines whether longs (backwardation/negative funding) or shorts (contango/positive funding) earn carry while holding. The book documents that roll profit/loss must be accounted separately from price-based signal P&L, and that carry (not forecasting skill) explains a large share of speculator profitability in the academic record.
trigger_invalidation: Carry is a passive return stream, not an entry trigger; the invalidation is sign reversal - backwardation flipping to contango flips the sign of the roll profit; the book notes seasonal commodities can move between contango and backwardation as supply tightens.
risk_geometry: Holding-period cost model item: roll profit enters the simulator cost/PnL model separately from the signal; in crypto perps this is the funding settlement line.

strategy_name: Positioning data segmentation integrity and indicator kill-switch
mechanism: Classifying long-only index/swap-dealer positions as 'commercials' fogged the true insider signal; when a structural change contaminates the segmentation, the indicator produces systematically invalid signals - and you must know your system well enough to recognize when it is not working and stop trading it.

strategy_name: Synthetic/composite positioning series construction
mechanism: For instruments without direct positioning data, construct a pseudo series by combining the sign-adjusted positioning of related, highly-correlated markets; a thin futures venue can still proxy global positioning because inter-dealer FX turnover is mostly offsetting 'hot potato' flow, not directional demand.

Validate the synthetic series against any thin native series (the EUR/JPY pseudo-COT matched the actual NYBOT series closely), and monitor correlations regularly since they drift and are not causal.

strategy_name: Passive-loser lifecycle rule (no natural game end -> mandatory predefined exit)
mechanism: unlike casino games, an open market position has no automatic end; doing nothing continues the loss, so every position must carry a pre-set loss limit, objective, and expiry enforced actively
setup_summary: Rule, not a signal: at entry, define the loss limit, the profit objective, and the conditions that end the position, because the market will not end it for you. A trader in a losing position must actively participate to stop the loss; inaction is a passive continuation of loss (down to liquidation).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any open position. Invalidation: position is closed only by the preplanned stop/target/expiry or dead-thesis exit, never by hope that the market 'comes back'.
risk_geometry: Entry: none (rule); stop: predefined loss limit set at entry; target: predefined objective; expiry: mandatory — no natural game end exists.
quote: In the market environment, you have to actively participate to get into a trade and actively participate to end your losses. If you do nothing, the potential exists to lose everything you own.

strategy_name: macro_release_avoidance
mechanism: the first minutes after a scheduled macro release are dominated by reactive/slippage-prone flow and headline-chasing; waiting for the actual number and planning on higher timeframes yields decisions based on fact rather than reaction
setup_summary: No new exposure during / immediately after a scheduled macro release (FOMC minutes, NFP, CPI) — the book's stated risk is that 'even no decision can move the dollar 100 points in sixty seconds.' After the number is known, plan on daily/weekly/4h charts ('You need to watch the longer term charts'), not 1-minute/tick charts, and let the trade play out over days-to-weeks, not minutes.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled high-impact release within the next few bars. Invalidation: rule is about entry suppression, not direction; it lapses once the release has printed and a plan is formed on longer timeframes.
risk_geometry: Entry: none during the avoid window (suppressed). Timeframe: the book prescribes daily/weekly/4-hour charts for planning ('the young guys are all looking at the five-minute charts, or God help them, the one-minute charts, or lower'), explicitly rejecting sub-hour planning.

strategy_name: Last buyer / public participation exhaustion (distribution top)
mechanism: A bull market requires continual infusion of new buyers; when participation broadens to the least risk-tolerant public and professionals begin distributing into them, the supply of marginal buyers runs out and the market has nowhere to go but down.
setup_summary: Near the end of a sustained rally, watch for participation broadening to the most risk-averse, latest-arriving traders - in perps, observable as extreme funding, crowded longs, surging new accounts and open interest. The professional 'knows the end is near' when the public buys en masse and starts taking profits while buyers still exist.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = broad late/public participation at price highs. Thesis (distribution top) invalidated if new buyers keep being drawn in and price keeps extending - the marginal-buyer pool is not yet exhausted.
risk_geometry: No mechanical entry/stop/target given; a sentiment/flow-based distribution signal, not a bar-level setup.
quote: When the last buyer has bought, the market has no place to go but down.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'High à Retrace à Rally to a Lower High' (public-participation discussion), pp.164-165
notes: The finite-buyer premise is structurally weaker in 24/7 global perp markets where new participants can enter at any hour, but retail crowding is directly observable in crypto via funding rate, long/short ratios and OI. Usable as a participation feature (input to risk/regime), not a standalone entry.
book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

strategy_name: Transaction-cost ratio scales inversely with target size
mechanism: spread/slippage is roughly fixed per trade while target size shrinks on lower timeframes, so short-horizon small-target trades carry disproportionately high transaction cost
setup_summary: Before choosing a timeframe, compute total round-trip cost / expected target. Worked example: 2-pip spread on a 10-pip scalp = 16% commission, versus 1.9% on a 100-pip daily target; a 3-pip slippage on a 10-pip target is a 30% profit cut that can tip a system into unprofitability.
trigger_invalidation: n/a (methodology constraint)
risk_geometry: n/a
quote: The spread on the EUR/USD is likely to be quite tight, perhaps two pips, so you must make 12 pips to bag 10 pips of profit. This is a commission of 16 percent... Longer-term trading is not only cheaper, it is easier to execute successfully.
chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Choosing Your Playing Field (pp. 225-226)
notes: Direct input to the V8 Binance USDM cost model and lab reporting: a per-trade cost/target ratio metric should gate which (target_r, expiry_bars) variants are viable on 1h BTCUSDT. Taker fees + funding + slippage are a fixed per-trade drag that eats small-target, short-expiry strategies.
book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

strategy_name: Contrarian at sentiment extremes
mechanism: Pessimism is the most common cause of low prices; crowd fear/greed extremes push prices away from fair value, then revert
setup_summary: When crowd sentiment reaches an extreme (observed proxies in perps: funding rate extremes, record open interest, lopsided long/short skew), fade the crowd direction. 'Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy only when others are fearful.' Falsifiable: entry opposite the sentiment extreme, hold for reversion toward the pre-extreme level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: participation/flow extremes at record percentiles. Invalidation: sentiment extreme persists and deepens (no reversion within window), i.e., the crowd is right.
risk_geometry: Book specifies no entry/stop/target; holding horizon years, not bars. For V8: needs bar-close entry, ATR or swing stop, expiry bars; the book's own warning is that a panic can stay extended in a leveraged venue.
quote: We simply attempt... to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Mr. Market), pp. 180-181
notes: Proxies (funding, OI, long/short skew) are directly observable 24/7 on perps, making this testable; but crypto has no intrinsic-value floor, so a pure sentiment fade without a value anchor can be killed by a leverage cascade (see deleveraging_cascade starter vocabulary). Gate as a sentiment feature input until participation/flow feature groups are formalized.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Crowding gate: consensus empties the edge
mechanism: When everyone makes the same choice for the same reason, no one is left to profit from it and the crowded position is vulnerable to a sharp unwind
setup_summary: When positioning/consensus becomes one-sided (mob influence, institutional imitation), the edge on that side evaporates and unwind risk rises. Falsifiable as a risk gate: block new entries on the crowded side when participation/flow extremes are present, or fade the crowded side; crowding proxies for perps are funding rate, open interest, and long/short skew.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: crowding metric at extreme percentile. Invalidation: consensus positions continue to be rewarded (crowding is not mean-reverting in this regime).
risk_geometry: Book specifies no geometry. As a gate: no entry on the crowded side; if used as an entry, contrarian with ATR/surplus stop, because the unwind move can be a liquidation cascade.
quote: when everyone is making the same choices because 'everyone' knows it's the thing to do, then no one is in a position to profit.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (temperament / mob influence), p. 179; institutional imperative referenced pp. 96-102
notes: Munger's institutional-imperative/herding claim. Highest perp relevance of the book: funding/OI/long-short crowding is measurable, and crowded perp positioning is exactly what produces liquidation cascades; this complements the existing liquidity/participation feature-group direction rather than a new price expert.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Avoid turnarounds / severe structural change
mechanism: assets undergoing major restructuring or directional change carry a high probability of major errors, so the expected return of such trades is impaired
setup_summary: Do not initiate positions in assets undergoing fundamental restructuring, turnaround, or major change; 'severe change and exceptional returns usually don't mix.' Prefer unchanged, consistent assets ('very much profiting from lack of change'). This rule constrains contrarian entries to temporary setbacks only and excludes broken or regime-changing assets from the universe.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger for avoidance: announced restructuring, turnaround, hostile-change, or structural regime shift in the candidate. Invalidation of the avoidance: the change completes and a consistent post-change track record re-establishes the asset as eligible.
risk_geometry: No entry by construction - acts as a pre-filter on the candidate universe; substitutes 'one-foot hurdles' selection over 'seven-footers' (no stop needed because the trade is never taken).
quote: Severe change and exceptional returns usually don't mix.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Business Tenets' (p.68, 'turnarounds seldom turn' p.67); Ch 3 textile turnaround lesson (p.30)
notes: For perp crypto: avoid catching falling knives in assets with structural breaks (chain hard-forks, regulatory bans, stablecoin de-pegs, exchange collapses). Complements the capitulation family by excluding broken assets - the two rules together define which fear-collapses are buyable. Buffett's Berkshire textile experience (closed 1985) is the canonical failure case.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Float economics / being paid to hold (funding carry)
mechanism: when the cost of holding capital is zero or negative - premiums exceed payouts - the holder is literally paid to hold, so carry turns a hold position into a positive-yield position
setup_summary: Insurers win when the cost of float is zero or negative; Berkshire's reinsurance group ran a negative 3% cost of float in 2003 (underwriting gain > $1B). Applied to perp: enter/hold positions only when expected edge clears funding + fees; when funding strongly favors the position side, carrying is itself a positive yield. Never 'write dumb policies' (negative-EV trades taken just to stay active).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: funding rate pays the position side and expected price move clears remaining costs. Invalidation: funding flips or carrying costs exceed edge - exit or refuse the position.
risk_geometry: Entry only if edge > funding + fee; holding favored while being paid; exit when carry turns negative relative to edge; no bar-level stop stated.
quote: The insurer is literally being paid to hold the capital.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Our Main Business Is Insurance' - float economics (p.35-37); 'dumb insurance policies' quote (p.38)
notes: Unique perp-crypto transfer: the funding rate is the direct analog of float cost. Two V8 landings: (1) funding as a mandatory cost in the simulator cost model and as a feature-group input (flow/time), and (2) funding-tailwind holding as a carry-family backlog candidate. Caution: funding is a small term vs. 1h price risk.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Validated seasonal cycle activated by a price trigger
mechanism: a seasonal cycle is only tradable if validated by out-of-sample correlation (Cycle-R) of exogenous data halves, and only executed when price confirms the direction via a trigger
setup_summary: Build a calendar-year seasonal cycle by compositing prior years; accept it only if Cycle-R (correlation between cycles built on the first vs second half of history, or across look-backs) is positive/meaningful (example given: 0.76 for SBUX); trade only the strongest (long) and weakest (short) zones of >=14 days and only in the cycle's direction, and only when a price trigger (e.g., close through the daily DMA channel) confirms the move. Seasonal heat (consistency across prior years' cycles) weights zone reliability.
trigger_invalidation: Setup invalid if Cycle-R is negative or seasonal heat is dark/inconsistent; trade invalidated when price closes back through the trigger level (e.g., the DMA channel).
risk_geometry: Entry/exit = close vs DMA channel. Worked example: AXP long entry $39.72, exit $45.86 (+15.46% in 38 trading days); short entry $42.30, exit $39.09 (+7.00% in 11 days); no ATR stop — channel-cross exit. Dow 30 tables show W/L improving 0.59->1.55->2.50->7.00 as validity and bias filters stack.
quote: it is wise to act on shifts in the seasonal patterns only if a price trigger indicates a move in the new direction of seasonality.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Testing for a Valid Seasonal Cycle' and 'Applying Cycles as a Strategy' (pp. 85-100)
notes: Evidence is single-year Dow 30 tables plus a correlation validity test — statistically presented but narrow. Calendar-year seasonality transfers weakly to crypto (no equity calendar, ~13y BTC history); the transferable methodology is (a) the Cycle-R out-of-sample validity gate before trusting any periodic pattern, and (b) the rule that a setup is only acted on with a price trigger. Hour-of-week / funding-cycle effects could be tested with the same validation discipline.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Accounting numbers are the beginning, not the end (source-integrity audit)
mechanism: Reported figures can be 'as pliable as putty'; certified numbers carry false precision, so investors must reconstruct economic reality from primary facts rather than accept reported earnings at face value.
setup_summary: For V8's marketstate and data pipeline: treat any vendor-reported or pre-computed series (funding rate, open interest, volume) as an 'accounting number' to be audited against the primary tape before it enters a PIT MarketState. Falsifiable: any feature group consumed by an expert must be reproducible from raw event-level data in the append-only store; series that cannot be reconstructed are excluded.
trigger_invalidation: Data-governance rule: a feature source that fails reconstruction from the primary tape is quarantined, regardless of how much edge it appears to add.
risk_geometry: N/A - pipeline discipline for src/v8/marketstate.py and the PIT builder; supports the three-clock (event/available/ingested) rule.
quote: investors must always keep their guard up and use accounting numbers as a beginning, not an end, in their attempts to calculate true 'economic earnings' accruing to them.
chapter_anchor: Part V.B Look-Through Earnings, p.168; V.G Deferred Taxes (the $1.1B liability-vs-trade-creditor contrast, p.194)
notes: Exchange-reported perp metrics (funding, OI, wash-inflated volume) are exactly the 'pliable putty' figures the book warns about; the look-through principle (judge by reconstructed economics, not reported line items) maps to V8's PIT reconstruction and source-integrity audit.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Hidden Correlation = Unrecognized Concentration
mechanism: exposures that look independent all correlate in a stress event; if you do not price the correlation you carry an unrecognized concentration of risk
setup_summary: Assume correlations go to 1 in a crisis before taking the book: 'when telecom debt collapsed, people found that all of it was correlated'; the subprime mortgage mess correlated across instruments Berkshire had never linked. For a perp book this means BTC/ETH/alt longs, funding carry, and basis positions are ONE risk in a crash, and heat must be capped as if one instrument - never by per-instrument or per-direction limits alone.
trigger_invalidation: Standing rule, not an episodic setup; it binds continuously and is strongest exactly when single-instrument risk measures look lowest.
risk_geometry: Aggregate book exposure cap computed under a correlation->1 stress assumption; do not rely on per-instrument diversification to reduce heat in the tail.
quote: When things go bad, all kinds of things correlate that you wouldn't think of. If you are not aware of these correlations, you have an unrecognized concentration of risk.
chapter_anchor: 2003 'Correlation'; 2005 'Correlation of Risk'
notes: Reuses starter slug correlated_exposure_cap. Strengthens the existing V8 one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule and the heat cap: the cap must aggregate under the assumption that all open exposures are one exposure in a cascade.

strategy_name: Be Greedy When Others Are Fearful (sentiment-extreme contrarian)
mechanism: extreme sentiment marks price far from value because the herd's emotion, not economics, drives the extreme; fading the extreme reverts when the emotional driver exhausts
setup_summary: Take the opposite side of emotional extremes: 'be fearful when others are greedy and greedy only when others are fearful'; Buffett and Munger bought through every crisis (2008, 2002 junk, 1974) while 'euphoria prevails' marked the tops. In perp crypto the measurable extremes are deeply negative funding, capitulation volume, flushed open interest, and record-low sentiment - a contrarian long setup that should be validated against the existing capitulation backlog family.
trigger_invalidation: The extreme does not revert while the reason for fear remains fundamentally valid - distinguish a liquidity/sentiment flush (tradeable) from a genuine thesis break (not tradeable); Buffett's 2008 muni dislocation reverted, the subprime mortgage decline did not.
risk_geometry: No stop given by the book; the margin of safety substitutes for a tight stop, so the setup requires the price-vs-value gap to be large before the extreme is faded.
quote: We simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
chapter_anchor: 1987 'On the Market' (annual-report quote); 2008 subprime/crisis commentary
notes: Reuses starter slug sentiment_extreme. Corroborates the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion); proposed behavior_family_candidate extreme_fear_reversal. Note: sentiment is not in the V8 feature-group vocabulary, so it must be proxied through participation/liquidity/flow features (volume climax, flushed OI, funding).

strategy_name: Herd head-fake (consensus theme displacement)
mechanism: When capital consensus herds into one technology theme while a dismissed alternative quietly scales, the herd position is the fragile one and the displaced alternative wins the repricing.
setup_summary: Lesson-level, not a tradable setup. In 1992-94 the world's largest media/software companies and their investors all herded into building the interactive-TV 'telecomputer' (SGI/Time Warner Orlando ITV, AT&T, Microsoft, Oracle); the actual winner was the ignored Internet (Netscape), which within six months made the entire herd look wrong. Crypto-perp analogue would be: extreme crowding into one narrative sector while an adjacent ignored narrative accrues volume/flow is a fragility signal, not a confirmation signal.
trigger_invalidation: Invalidated if consensus-crowded themes systematically outperform displaced alternatives in follow-on repricings.
risk_geometry: None stated; the book describes an allocation-level event, not an entry/stop/target structure.
quote: Then, just as they all ran as a herd in one direction, he took off in another. And within six months he made them all look like fools. It was one of the great unintentional head fakes in the history of technology.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Inventing Jim Clark'
notes: n=1 event in equity capital allocation; no price-level mechanism stated, so it cannot be formalized as an expert today. At most a qualitative warning: consensus crowding as anti-confirmation for narrative trades (funding/long-bias extremes).

strategy_name: Consensus-exhausted announcement reversal (sell-the-news / market-not-following-news)
mechanism: When analysts have talked up a consensus outcome and the market has already moved in that direction before the announcement, post-announcement follow-through fails and profit-taking reverses price
setup_summary: Before a scheduled announcement, if expectations are widely known, analysts have talked up figures excessively, and price has already run in the expected direction, fade the post-announcement continuation: anticipate a quick selloff/bounce against the consensus. Book's crude-oil inventory case: bearish inventory news dropped price one day, then price broke out to new highs.
trigger_invalidation: If the actual number surprises beyond consensus, momentum continues with the news and the reversal thesis fails.
risk_geometry: Reversal entry after the event print; stop beyond the pre-event range; book example target was a large extension (~$11/bbl over ~2 weeks on crude).
quote: If the news was bullish, but the analyst had already predicted that, and the market had already made gains up until the announcement, then we could see a quick selloff.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 Event-Based Trading Examples pp. 80-88
notes: For crypto: funding-rate/positioning extremes plus consensus macro narrative before CPI/FOMC. Inversion signal = pre-event run-up magnitude relative to consensus. Would need a scheduled-event + funding/positioning feature set (time, flow groups).
